pluss::subsp::stats::ts::MvGarch¶

Fits a constant-conditional-correlation model with a GARCH variance for every series.

Signature¶

ts::MvGarchFit ts::MvGarch::fit_mle(const pluss::Series& y, const ts::MvGarchOptions& options = {}, pluss::codem::Config cfg = {});

Construction¶

MvGarch has no instances: it is a namespace for the static fit_mle, which returns an MvGarchFit.

Methods¶

fit_mle¶

ts::MvGarchFit ts::MvGarch::fit_mle(const pluss::Series& y, const ts::MvGarchOptions& options = {}, pluss::codem::Config cfg = {});

Fits the model in two stages. First a univariate Garch model is fitted to each column of y. Then the standardised residuals of all columns are correlated to give a constant correlation matrix; the covariance of series i and j at time t is then corr[i][j] · sqrt(h_i,t · h_j,t). The correlation is estimated from the standardised residuals after the marginals are fitted, optionally shrunk towards the identity.

const pluss::Series& y

The returns as an n × k matrix, one column per series.

const ts::MvGarchOptions& options

Options of the univariate models and of the correlation; see MvGarchOptions.

pluss::codem::Config cfg

Output configuration (dtype and platform of the returned series); computation is in double precision.

Returns. An MvGarchFit.

Errors. y must have at least 8 rows.

Practical Examples¶

Example 1¶

Fit two series with correlated shocks (true correlation 0.6) and read the estimated correlation and the log-likelihood.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
Series pair(int n) {
  std::vector<double> y(2 * n);
  double h1 = 0.4, h2 = 0.4, p1 = 0.0, p2 = 0.0;
  for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (t + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453, w = std::sin(12.9898 * (t + 40001.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    w -= std::floor(w);
    const double z1 = (u - 0.5) * std::sqrt(12.0), z2 = (w - 0.5) * std::sqrt(12.0);
    h1 = 0.05 + 0.15 * p1 * p1 + 0.75 * h1;
    h2 = 0.10 + 0.10 * p2 * p2 + 0.80 * h2;
    p1 = std::sqrt(h1) * z1;
    p2 = std::sqrt(h2) * (0.6 * z1 + 0.8 * z2);
    y[2 * t] = p1;
    y[2 * t + 1] = p2;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(y, {n, 2}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const Series y = pair(1500);
  const auto fit = ts::MvGarch::fit_mle(y);
  const auto corr = fit.corr.host<double>();
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(3) << "estimated correlation " << corr[1] << ", log-likelihood " << fit.loglik(y) << "\n";
}

Output

estimated correlation 0.612, log-likelihood -3338.318
